newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast power steady ahead of cooler temps.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast power steady ahead of cooler temps.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the southeastern U.S. held steady Tuesday against Monday's level ahead of cooler temperatures returning to the region later this week.
"It's nice down here today. It might go a little higher with the cooler weather," a Southeast marketer.
Wholesale power trading in the Southeast was light today with a number of participants still attending an industry conference in New Orleans, market sources said.
The ongoing rally in natural gas prices had little effect on daily prices in the Southeast, marketers said.
"Gas prices for next month have had impact on the forward months," a Houston trader noted.
NYMEX December Henry Hub natgas futures soared 18.2 cents to $3.160 per million British thermal units in afternoon trading.
Tennessee Valley Authority's (TVA) Sequoyah 1 nuclear power unit in Soddy-Daisy, Tenn., was holding output at 55 percent of its 1,148 megawatt (MW) capacity following a weekend outage.
TVA, the largest utility in the U.S., reportedly offered next-day power during heavy demand hours near $19.50 a megawatt hour (MWh) and during light demand hours near $16.00.
Peak, firm electricity for Wednesday delivery into the northwestern part of TVA territory was still assessed at $17.00-$18.00 per MWh.
Firm delivery during light-load hours on Wednesday was again pegged at $13.00-$15.00.
Down at the Georgia/Florida border, next-day electricity for firm, peak delivery was valued at $21.00-$23.00, flat from Monday's range.
Firm, off-peak Ga./Fla. power deliveries for Wednesday were assessed at $17.00-$18.00, unchanged from Monday.

In the Florida pennisula, 12-hour block power scheduled among the state's utilities for Wednesday was heard discussed at $24.00-$25.00, compared with Monday's $23.00-$25.50 for Tuesday. Meanwhile, 16-hour blocks were notationally talked in the $22.00-$23.00 area.

For Wednesday, temperatures in the Southeastern Electric Reliability Council (SERC) district were anticipated to peak in 50s-70s Fahrenheit and bottom in the 30s-50s, and those in Florida were predicted to peak in the 70s-80s and bottom in the 50s-60s.
Outlook for the rest of the week showed the northern part of SERC was forecast to receive cooler-than-normal weather, while southern SERC and most of Florida seasonal weather.
